text: The white man had known Arsat. <break time="0.8s" /> Years before in a distant country. <break time="0.8s" /> In times of trouble and danger. <break time="0.8s" /> And he had come to value. <break time="0.8s" /> The young mans courage and loyalty. <break time="0.8s" /> Since then. <break time="0.8s" /> He had often stopped at this house. <break time="0.8s" /> On his journeys. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet he had never heard. <break time="0.8s" /> How Arsat and the woman. <break time="0.8s" /> Had come to live hidden in such a place. <break time="0.8s" /> The sun went down. <break time="0.8s" /> Darkness fell swiftly over the lagoon. <break time="0.8s" /> And the white man, sitting outside. <break time="0.8s" /> By a fire he had made. <break time="0.8s" /> To keep off the mosquitoes. <break time="0.8s" /> Watched the stars appear. <break time="0.8s" /> Far away across the water. <break time="0.8s" /> The voices of the boatmen. <break time="0.8s" /> Died out one by one. <break time="0.8s" /> And soon the whole world. <break time="0.8s" /> Seemed empty and silent. <break time="0.8s" /> Under the cold light of the stars. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking of the dying woman. <break time="0.8s" /> The white man felt in the darkness. <break time="0.8s" /> A strange mixture of fear and fascination. <break time="0.8s" /> As if the land around him. <break time="0.8s" /> Were a battlefield of phantoms. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Arsat came out. <break time="0.8s" /> And sat down by the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> And after a long silence he asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Tuan, do you remember my brother. <break time="0.8s" /> And the white man answered simply, Yes. <break time="0.8s" /> Tuan, I must tell you everything. <break time="0.8s" /> Arsat began softly. <break time="0.8s" /> For a man should share his sorrow. <break time="0.8s" /> With a friend. <break time="0.8s" /> And what the eye has seen is truth. <break time="0.8s" /> Long ago, he said. <break time="0.8s" /> He and his brother had served. <break time="0.8s" /> As sword bearers to the Ruler of their country. <break time="0.8s" /> And in those peaceful days. <break time="0.8s" /> He had fallen secretly in love with Diamelen. <break time="0.8s" /> She was a servant of Inchi Midah. <break time="0.8s" /> The Rulers wife. <break time="0.8s" /> So that the lovers could meet only. <break time="0.8s" /> In quick glances. <break time="0.8s" /> And in whispers behind the flowering hedges.
